title: Freedom Yield Metal — Incidents Audit Packet v1
description: Formal contract for /api/incidents.json. Records operator-visible events affecting the validator host, the public web, the monitoring pipeline, or the on-chain validator entry. Three event categories are kept in one stream and distinguished by 'type': 'incident' (unintended condition), 'scheduled_maintenance' (planned operator work, announced ahead), 'drill' (deliberate exercise of a runbook). Severity classification uses the Critical/Major/Minor/Info taxonomy displayed on /incidents/; the SEV-1..4 mapping documented in docs/INCIDENT_RESPONSE.md is internal. potentiallyAffectedStart is null when undetermined; the separate potentiallyAffectedStartStatus enum distinguishes 'known' / 'undetermined' / 'not_applicable'. confirmedPauseWindowEnd is null while the window is still ongoing. resolutionDate is null while the event is open or under_remediation. Schema is additive-only-within-v1; breaking changes require /api/incidents.schema.v2.json. The v1 URL stays reachable for at least 18 months after v2 publication.

_comment.description: Free-form human-readable preamble. Consumers MAY ignore.

validatorSince.description: ISO 8601 date when the validator went live on mainnet. Used by readers as a denominator for incident-rate calculations.

incidents.description: Append-only list. Existing entries SHOULD NOT be removed; entries can be updated in-place to advance status / add resolutionDate / link a postmortem. Order is newest-first by detectionDate per page rendering convention.

id.description: Stable identifier in YYYY-MM-DD-NN form. NN is a per-day sequence (01, 02, ...) so two events detected the same day each get a distinct id.

type.description: Event category. 'incident' = unintended condition. 'scheduled_maintenance' = planned, announced ahead. 'drill' = deliberate runbook exercise.

detectionDate.description: ISO date when the operator first became aware of the condition (for incidents) or began the planned operation (for scheduled_maintenance / drill).

confirmedPauseWindowStart.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp marking the start of a confirmed pause / unavailability window. Null when not applicable (e.g. event has no observable pause).

confirmedPauseWindowEnd.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp marking the end of the confirmed pause window. Null while the window is still ongoing.

potentiallyAffectedStart.description: ISO date marking the earliest plausible start of impact. MUST be null when the start cannot be reconstructed from records reviewed; use the companion potentiallyAffectedStartStatus to disambiguate. Plain string sentinels like 'undetermined' are NOT permitted — use null + status.

potentiallyAffectedStartStatus.description: Disambiguates potentiallyAffectedStart=null. 'known' = the date in potentiallyAffectedStart is reliable. 'undetermined' = potentiallyAffectedStart is null because the start could not be reconstructed from records reviewed. 'not_applicable' = the event type has no notion of an affected-start (e.g. scheduled_maintenance with no impact).

resolutionDate.description: ISO date when the event was marked resolved. Null while status is 'open' or 'under_remediation'.

severity.description: Public severity class per /incidents/ taxonomy. Critical = key compromise or validator down 24h+. Major = site down or metalgo down 4h+. Minor = TLS warnings, transient degradation. Info = configuration change or planned maintenance. Internal SEV-1..4 mapping is documented in docs/INCIDENT_RESPONSE.md and is NOT exposed in this schema.

status.description: Workflow status. 'open' = newly detected, not yet being actively remediated. 'under_remediation' = operator is working on it. 'resolved' = closed, no further action expected.

summary.description: 1-3 sentence human-readable summary suitable for rendering on /incidents/. SHOULD be hedged when the impact is not fully reconstructed (e.g. 'records reviewed do not indicate impact' rather than 'no impact occurred').

postmortemUrl.description: Link to the technical postmortem. Null while the postmortem has not been published. URL is typically a docs/POSTMORTEM_*.md path on the public repo.
